context_notes: The through-line of BOTH tasks this session is that a gate which LOOKS like coverage and asserts NOTHING is caught only by an independent pass, never by its author -- and that fixes need reviewing as hard as originals. Five instances: lc3's SRV-05 cardinality gate (satisfiable by deletion); lpt's six vacuous presence gates, found by the author applying 'would writing NOTHING pass?' to the ADDITIVE direction; lpt's dead G7b, whose literal spanned a line wrap so it could never match while being the only guard on a stale value; lpt's false 'twenty boxes' claim headed INTO the sealed audit the task exists to make accurate; and lpt's G8, added to close a prose-only hole, which both under-enforced (passed on a section with zero quotes) and false-failed (tripped on legitimate downstream text). The last one is the sharpest lesson: the unbounded-region rule was SAFE where iteration 1 checked it because those sections append at EOF, and was carried to a MID-FILE section without adapting the bound. Same rule, different position, opposite outcome. Also carry forward three measured false-zero shapes, all of which read as confident absence: (1) a literal spanning a line wrap; (2) `rg -U` with `\s+` cannot bridge a wrap whose continuation carries a '#' -- use `[\s#]+`; (3) a SHAPE-anchored regex like `^\| (CORR-05|RETAIN-05) ` returns exit 1 because the target file records verdicts as headings rather than table rows. And `git grep` needs `-e` when the pattern starts with `-`: `git grep -n -F '- [ ]' -- f` fails with 'error: unknown switch'. Finally: the audit's own item-7 list caught 6 of 20 instances of one defect -- it undercounted Phase 13 (six, not five), omitted Phases 10 and 11 entirely, and miscounted Phase 10 as seven rows when it has eight. An item list that finds 30 percent of one defect class is the interesting result, and it is recorded in the plan as a finding about the AUDIT's completeness.
